findings.question: logp-predicate-q6
findings.original: This says no A is a B, which is far stronger than "not every A is a B". The quantifier must flip to ∃.
findings.correction: This says no A is a B. It is not equivalent to the negation: with no A objects it is vacuously true, while not-every-A-is-B is false. If A objects exist, it requires all of them to fail B rather than just one.
findings.reason: Vacuous truth defeats claimed unconditional stronger relation.

findings.original: A brute-force search would only ever give you evidence; the case split gives certainty in four lines.
findings.correction: A bounded search over many target integers would not prove the universal claim. For one fixed nonnegative target, exhaustive search over bounded candidate squares can prove that target has no representation; the case split handles all targets at once.
findings.reason: Finite exhaustive search can prove individual impossibility.

findings.original: If your "contradiction" turns out to be "so ¬p, contradicting p", you have written a contrapositive proof; restate it that way, because it is cleaner.
findings.correction: If the derivation of ¬p uses only ¬q and background facts, without relying on the additional assumption p, it can be restated as a direct contrapositive proof. Otherwise it remains a contradiction argument.
findings.reason: Derivation depending on p cannot merely drop p premise.

findings.question: logp-induction-q10

findings.correction: Induction on size can work, commonly by assuming the property for all smaller expressions, or by strengthening an ordinary-induction statement. This answer does not enumerate the required structural cases.
findings.reason: Size induction need not exclusively be strong induction.

limitations: All six lesson bodies and all 73 complete question records independently read, including answer keys, distractors, explanations and worked examples. Targeted primary-source checks complement mathematical reasoning; this is not an exhaustive sentence-to-source mapping.

Root harness independently inspected and rerun after verifier corrections: all 10 lesson Python fences, 10 quiz Python fences and 2 SQL fences executed with contextual fixtures. SQLite SQL execution does not test PostgreSQL-specific runtime behavior.

Finite exhaustive and randomized checks support the examples but do not prove all mathematical claims. No industrial SAT benchmark, production SMT deployment, Dafny run, TLA+ model-checking run or RSA timing was performed.

Primary documents confirm Gelfond-Schneider theorem, Eclipse p2 SAT4J, MiniSat backjump handling, DRAT, AWS formal-methods experience and current Collatz status. Some standard historical attribution was semantically reviewed without archival retrieval. Initial AWS SMT paper retrieval failed; official AWS article used as fallback.

Three unsupported empirical/model-generalization claim categories remain visibly omitted in lessons: fixed RSA timing, universal SAT solve/verification timing, and universal density-based easy/hard cutoff. These author omissions were independently reviewed and retained.
